doc.title: John Heard interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995

title: Musicians he learned from, good and bad
summary: He says you learn from everybody and lists pianists, bandleaders, singers and pop groups he listened to.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: And what kind of people did you listen to? I mean was there guys on records that you tried to learn from?
Oh, everybody. You learn from everybody. Even the ones that are terrible.
You learn what not to play — I’m not going to play like that.

No, I’ve had many experiences. Ahmad Jamal, Errol Garner, Art Blakey, Count Basie, Ella Fitzgerald, Louis Armstrong, you know, it goes on and on, Charlie Mingus, you know, and Shearing. Dave Brubeck, he had that big hit when I was in high school. Ellington, everybody. I learned from everybody, you know? Ervin, Billy Eckstine, they were all you know, they were making music in those days. They were nice times. Even Theresa Brewer and Frankie Laine, I listened to them, you know? The Four Lads, The Platters, the Dominoes, Fats Domino, all of it. Delta River Boys, right?
